Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from the first Test where West Indies took a 1-0 lead with a commanding effort over Bangladesh. The Windies will want to seal the series while the Tigers will hope they can roar back and finish on level terms. The 2nd Test will be played at the Sabina Park in Kingston, Jamaica. The first day is scheduled for 30th November, Saturday at 3 pm GMT, but as you know, you can always join us early for all the build-up. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

Kraigg Brathwaite, the victorious skipper of West Indies says that there has been a lot of learning over time, especially from the series against England and it is good to see the improvements and they will only look to build from here on. Adds that they have quality fast bowlers and with Justin in the squad it adds more depth and with different skill sets it is a great sign for the team. Mentions that the talk to the boys will be to stay focused, put this game behind and keep improving and growing in confidence. Concludes by thanking the fans for the support they showed.

Mehidy Hasan, the captain of Bangladesh says that they bowled really well in this game but batting was not up to the mark. Praises Taskin Ahmed for his maiden Test fifer. Adds that they made a few mistakes in this match and hopes that they can learn from them and come back stronger in the next one. Mentions that they have a great pace unit of Taskin, Hasan Mahmud, and Nahid Rana who have done well in the last few years, and in the spin department, Taijul Islam has performed well too. Ends by saying that they will need to focus on the areas to improve and will want to execute the plans better in the next match.

Justin Greaves is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his fantastic unbeaten ton and 2 wickets. He says contributing to the team in a winning cause is a special feeling. Mentions that he had a plan on how to bat with the rest of the unit and he is glad to have contributed. Adds that Kraigg Brathwaite backs him a lot and lets him express himself freely which is a big plus and he believes in himself to keep going.
Presentation Time...

The entire pace unit of the West Indies is down for a chat. Kemar Roach starts and says he is very proud of the group they have and with Justin coming in with his skills it makes it stronger. Alzarri Joseph mentions that they as a group try and help each other and they have a healthy challenge among each other too. Jayden Seales adds that they are well-complimented by the pace of Alzarri and Sharmar while the rest three try and pile on the pressure. Justin Greaves mentions his role in this group and says they expect him to just keep things tight and hold the tight line. Shamar Joseph says that it is a great experience to be a part of this group and he has watched Kemar and Alzarri when he hadn't even thought of playing cricket and has been welcomed really nicely into the side and gets to learn a lot. Kemar concludes that the fans can expect them to come back with the same intensity and do it all over again in the next game.

Bangladesh’s bold overnight declaration turned the game on its head, as their bowlers, led by a fiery Taskin Ahmed, dismantled the Windies for just 152, setting up a thrilling chase of 334. Taskin was unplayable, claiming a sensational maiden five-wicket haul and finishing with 6 scalps, while Mehidy Hasan chipped in with crucial breakthroughs. A stunning collapse saw the hosts lose 7 wickets for just 63 runs, giving the Tigers a real shot at glory. But the chase began disastrously - Kemar Roach’s relentless pace rocked the top order, and with Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph joining the onslaught, Bangladesh were left reeling at 59/5. Skipper Mehidy fought valiantly with a gritty 45, but his dismissal late in the day, coupled with another strike, left Bangladesh on the brink, needing a miracle to pull off a historic win.

Bangladesh showed incredible resilience, battling hard against a fiery Windies attack despite early setbacks. Kemar Roach’s breakthrough and Alzarri Joseph’s fiery spells tested their mettle, but Mominul Haque’s gritty fifty and Litton Das’s intent-filled 76-ball knock kept the visitors in the fight. After their dismissals, skipper Mehidy Hasan and Jaker Ali absorbed relentless pressure, forging a vital 50-plus stand. Ali’s spirited half-century and Taijul Islam’s support guided Bangladesh past the follow-on mark, with some luck as the Windies missed chances. Even as Justin Greaves struck late and grabbed his best Test figures, Bangladesh clung on under fading light, setting up a thrilling Day 4 in this gripping contest!

Bangladesh began with fire on Day 2, as Hasan Mahmud struck twice in quick succession, igniting hopes of restricting the Windies under 300. But Justin Greaves was the star of the day, crafting a magnificent maiden Test century in a defiant 140-run stand with Kemar Roach, whose valiant 47 frustrated the visitors. Taskin Ahmed’s missed chance proved costly, as the Windies piled on the runs. Late fireworks from Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph propelled the hosts to a commanding declaration at 450/9, with Greaves unbeaten on a glorious 115. In reply, Bangladesh’s openers faced hostile spells, with Zakir Hasan and Mahmudul Hasan Joy falling to fiery deliveries from Seales and Alzarri Joseph. Under immense pressure, Shahadat Hossain and Mominul Haque showed remarkable resilience, battling through to Stumps to keep Bangladesh’s hopes alive in this high-stakes clash!

Bangladesh’s decision to bowl first paid early dividends as their pacers, led by Taskin Ahmed, broke through with vital strikes to dismiss Kraigg Brathwaite and Keacy Carty. However, the day belonged to the resilient Mikyle Louis, whose gritty 90 anchored the West Indies' fightback. Louis, alongside Kavem Hodge and later Alick Athanaze, steadied the innings with crucial partnerships, countering Bangladesh’s relentless attack. Despite a nerve-wracking fall in the 90s for both set batters, Joshua Da Silva and Justin Greaves launched a spirited late assault, blunting the second new ball to take the hosts to stumps in control.

The final day began with Bangladesh facing an uphill battle, needing a miracle, while the West Indies were just three wickets away. Alzarri Joseph wasted no time, dismissing Hasan Mahmud early before removing Jaker Ali, the last recognized batter. Moments later, a fiery bouncer struck Shoriful Islam on the neck, forcing him to retire hurt, sealing an emphatic 201-run victory for the Windies. Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales were instrumental on Day 4 dismantling the Bangladeshi batting line-up, sharing 6 wickets equally while Shamar Joseph chipped in with one. For Bangladesh's batting point of view, Mehidy Hasan, Mominul Haque, and Jaker Ali were the only ones who looked up to the task, but they still have a lot of work to do to challenge quality teams in this format.

West Indies have secured a wonderful Test victory, taking a 1-0 lead in the series! This is also their 7th consecutive Test win over Bangladesh at home showing their dominance over them. Their performance throughout the game was commanding, and this win is well-deserved. While Bangladesh displayed glimpses of resilience and determination, their batting woes once again proved to be their undoing.

Halt! Earlier, Shoriful Islam got hit on the back of the neck, and now the physio is out to conduct a concussion check on him. Oh..no! It does not look like he will be able to continue, and the players are shaking hands at the moment. Wow! That is an anti-climactic end to the game but safety does come first and we hope that Shoriful Islam recovers quickly. WEST INDIES WIN BY 201 RUNS!

A bye taken and more importantly it will be Taskin Ahmed on strike for the next over!

Commentary.Commentary: In all readiness for the action to begin on this final day! The two umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed by Jaker Ali and Hasan Mahmud who are up and ready to resume their overnight stay for Bangladesh. Jayden Seales is handed the ball and will start the proceedings on this concluding day for the West Indies! Away we go!

Shamar Joseph is down for a chat. He says it is nice to be here and mentions that he tried to keep the lines and lengths consistent and says the plan against Litton Das was to bowl short but not overdo it. Adds that Alzarri Joseph asked him to stick to his basics and forget everything that has gone past. Concludes that they as a fast-bowling group they enjoy each other's success and keep encouraging one another.

The West Indies pace attack has been nothing short of ferocious, consistently applying unrelenting pressure on the Bangladesh batters. However, despite their dominance, a few dropped chances and lapses in the field remain an area they’d want to improve. Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales have spearheaded the attack brilliantly and will aim to finish the job early by capitalizing on the opening half-hour of play. While the victory seems well within their grasp, West Indies will be keen to maintain their intensity and ensure there’s no room for a Bangladesh resurgence. Stay with us as we gear up for an exciting conclusion to this Test match which is just moments away from resumption!

There’s been plenty of debate surrounding Bangladesh’s bold decision to declare their innings while trailing by 181 runs with a wicket in hand. In hindsight, it seems like a gamble that didn’t fully pay off. However, credit must be given to their bowlers, who put in a spirited effort in the third innings, delivering with heart and precision to pull back a contest that seemed to be slipping away entirely. Despite their bowlers’ heroics, Bangladesh’s batting remains a glaring concern. A lack of application and the inability to build partnerships has cost them dearly in this Test, and it’s an area they’ll need to address moving forward. With just three wickets in hand, avoiding defeat will take nothing short of a miracle. Realistically, it looks like an uphill battle, but cricket has a way of throwing up surprises and Bangladesh will hope for that.

Hello and a warm welcome to the final day of this riveting first Test between West Indies and Bangladesh, coming to you from the iconic Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Antigua! West Indies have been in command for the majority of this match and are now on the verge of sealing a well-deserved victory to go 1-0 up in this two-match series. Requiring just three more wickets and holding a hefty cushion of 224 runs to defend, the hosts are staring at what seems like a straightforward path to victory.
... DAY 5, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an enthralling Day 4 of this first Test. West Indies are on the verge of a victory here and will be looking to wrap things up quickly on the final day while for Bangladesh, it is all about survival. Day 5 will start at 2 pm GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Taskin Ahmed is up for a quick. He says that it is very special to him to get his first 5-wicket haul in Test cricket. Adds that he bowled just okayish in the first innings and learned many things which he applied in the second one like altering lines and lengths. Mentions that the bowlers get an advantage because of the strong breeze, and that did help him in getting his breakthroughs. Concludes by saying that despite their fightback, they are unfortunately seven down in the chase and will come back harder next time.

Bangladesh’s big chase got off to a nightmare start in the final session, undone by a relentless West Indies bowling attack. Kemar Roach was unstoppable, striking in the very first over to remove Zakir Hasan and ending with three scalps, taking his tally to 54 Test wickets on this ground. Jayden Seales and Shamar Joseph joined the carnage, reducing Bangladesh to 59/5. Litton Das and Mominul Haque couldn’t capitalize on their starts, while skipper Mehidy Hasan fought back with a gutsy 45, playing positive cricket despite some luck. Just as he steadied the ship with Jaker Ali, his dismissal and a late strike from Seales left Bangladesh reeling, staring at the brink of defeat as bad light ended play.

It was a great turnaround by Bangladesh! Their bold declaration paid off spectacularly, bundling the hosts out for just 152 and setting up a thrilling chase of 334 runs. Taskin Ahmed was absolutely unplayable, ripping through the West Indies lineup with a sensational 6-wicket haul including his maiden five-fer in Tests, while Mehidy Hasan chipped in with two key scalps. The Windies showed some fight before Lunch, but once Taskin struck again, it triggered a stunning collapse - 7 wickets fell for just 63 runs! Bangladesh certainly had time on their side but this chase required a series of good partnerships and nerves of steel.

Bangladesh made a bold overnight declaration despite a massive 181-run deficit, and backed it up brilliantly with the ball! Taskin Ahmed struck early to remove Mikyle Louis and Keacy Carty, while Shoriful Islam landed the crucial blow by dismissing Kraigg Brathwaite. The Tigers’ fiery energy kept the Windies under pressure, though a few missed chances left room for improvement. West Indies started with a bang, smashing 10 runs in the first over, but soon found themselves struggling to build partnerships and three down before Lunch, but still had a significant lead.

STUMPS ON DAY 4! SESSION SUMMARY - 109 runs and 7 wickets in 31 overs! A total of 17 wickets fell in the day, which is a record high at this ground! Despite Bangladesh’s brilliant bowling display in the third innings, Day 4 firmly belonged to the West Indies, thanks to their commanding first-innings lead. Their decision to field four seamers proved to be a masterstroke, with Kemar Roach and Jayden Seales leading the charge and outshining their counterparts by a considerable margin. With a dominant performance, the Windies now have one foot firmly over the finish line.

Another reading is being taken now and on both ends! Oh..no! This time the reading is not a good one, and the umpires give the marching orders to the players. So, that concludes play on the fourth day and we will be going to the final day with Bangladesh needing 225 runs with only 3 wickets in hand.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! West Indies have dominated the session so far sending half of the Bangladeshi batters back to the hut. Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! West Indies have stormed back into the game with a sensational display of pace bowling, completely dismantling the momentum Bangladesh carried into the break. The hosts have been relentless, hitting the right areas with precision and extracting every bit of assistance from the surface to have Bangladesh reeling at 20/3. Bangladesh now find themselves under immense pressure and in a desperate need of a partnership that can steady the nerves. Litton Das walks out to bat next!

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! An excellent review from West Indies and Kemar Roach gets his second wicket. He hits the length hard this time and around off again, gets it to jag back in sharply. Shahadat Hossain stays in his crease and tries to play it away from his body as the ball goes past the inside edge to the keeper where Joshua Da Silva makes no mistake. There is a bit of a noise and a massive shout for caught behind, but the umpire says no! Shahadat Hossain indicates that it has hit his arm, but Kraigg Brathwaite takes the review here. UltraEdge shows a spike when the ball is close to the gloves and the replay shows that it brushes against it before hitting the forearm. Hossain has to walk back now and Bangladesh are 20/3!
